thread.title: Why I Rotated Out Of Helios And Matheson Into Smith Micro And 2 Other Stocks At Key Inflection Points - Smith Micro Software, Inc. (NASDAQ:SMSI)

author: Ben Rabizadeh
title: Why I Rotated Out Of Helios And Matheson Into Smith Micro And 2 Other Stocks At Key Inflection Points - Smith Micro Software, Inc. (NASDAQ:SMSI)
text:
As many in the investment community are aware, MoviePass [via Helios and Matheson ( HMNY )], was my big speculative play which I wrote about extensively here , here , here , and here . For a while it worked out as myself and many others rode the wave from $3 to $38 (I initially heard about MoviePass at around $10 on its way up) but in the end, nearly everyone lost their gains on the stock. My initial bull thesis was based on the four pillars of a great investment: Brand , Industry , Management , and Moat - and all seemed to check out.
However the Management portion of this formula changed for the worse on April 17th when Ted Farnsworth pumped the stock talking about a $375M "line of credit" which turned out to be just the pre-existing shelf offering . I found this to be extremely dishonest and in fact perhaps even criminal - especially after a pattern of other management claims which turned out to be false. This prompted me to sell most of my position at $4.50 on that day. I wrote about my change of heart here. I didn't sell my entire position on that day but I managed to sell over 75% of my common stock before the financing on the next day and I liquidated my final shares at just above $2 the morning this 8-K came out warning shareholders that credit card companies were withholding funds from upfront annual fee plans. On that morning, I also went short via puts and rode the stock down to below $1. Given the fast moving nature of events, I wasn't able to publish an article about this move but I did telegraph it widely on StockTwits and on my whatsapp groups available at StoryTrading.com.
At present, I have no position in HMNY other than some worthless call options and I do not plan on getting back in until the story changes for the better. I do believe MoviePass may still succeed but due to the death-spiral nature of their current ATM financing, HMNY might first go down to sub-pennies before it goes on a 1,000% run. I do believe significant near-term risk remains including the possibility of lawsuits and SEC action against the company so I will simply watch things as an outsider for now and will react accordingly when the next news (good or bad) hits.
While in the end, I lost a nice chunk of money on HMNY, I did save most of my speculative investment money by selling far above the current share price . This kept me in the game and allowed me to reinvest in other areas. One thing I've learned in my years of investing is that you don't need to make your money back on the same stock. Accordingly, I used my HMNY assets to increase my positions in three promising stocks on the cusp of significant turn-arounds. I telegraphed this move here when I sold HMNY at $4.50 and increased my position in Smith Micro Software ( SMSI ) at around $2.
Three Stocks at the Inflection Point to Profitability
Company The Story Market Cap 2017 Sales Flip to Profitability SMSI Safe & Found product ramp up with Sprint ( S ) $55M $23M Q2/Q3 2018 Aehr Test Systems ( AEHR ) Undervalued business with 176% YoY growth already reported in Q1 $58M $19M already flipped to profitability in Q1 but additional significant upside to the bottom line will start Q3 2018 Chanticleer Holdings ( BURG ) High margin and scalable Little Big Burger 80% YoY store growth as franchising kicks in $11M $41M Q4 2018 / Q1 2019 I want to give you an idea of how microcap stocks perform after flipping to profitability. Zynex Medical ( OTCQB:ZYXI ) is a medical device company which was trading near $0.50 and a $20M market cap for years. Then when it flipped to profitability (and sustained the profitability), the stock moved 1,000% in just 6 months! Below is the chart so you can see how that looks. I've also marked on the chart where I think SMSI, AEHR, and BURG are relative to ZYXI's history.
BREAKING: As I was just about to submit this article, I learned that OakRidge financial just initiated coverage on BURG on June 5th with a $5 target but the catalysts are most near-term for SMSI, so I will focus on their story in today's article and cover AEHR and BURG in the future.
The SMSI Story SMSI is a software services company primarily serving wireless service providers for decades. The CEO, Bill Smith increased his stake last year to 29% and they announced their largest customer to date, Sprint, on October 13, 2017. It's taken six months for that relationship to ramp up and it's now in full force with Sprint marketing SMSI's product, SafePath , heavily to new Sprint customers.
This SafePath product is marketed as Safe & Found by Sprint. You can find the Sprint sales page for it here . The app is available on Apple and Google smartphones so you can track its growth from data providers like AppAnnie . Sprint has just started actively marketing this product in stores:
What's great about this relationship is that Sprint already has an installed userbase of 350,000 customers for their legacy safety product which will be transferred to the new service and based on data which can be gleaned, SMSI will receive a license fee of $3.50 per month for each subscriber!
That's an additional $14M revenue per year just from Sprint's installed user base porting over! In addition to this, Sprint has said they are targeting millions of new subscribers for Safe & Found. Take a look at this math... there are over 4,500 Sprint stores. If each store signed up just five additional new customers a week, that would be an additional $49M in annual revenue at 70-80% margins (which the CEO has affirmed on multiple occasions). It's no wonder analyst, Mark Gomes, is forecasting $0.81 in EPS by 2020 which would mean a stock price of $16 with a 20 PE.
The catalysts are piling up. SMSI recently did an above-market offering ... money which they did not need but which was offered to them by investors per comments made by the CEO at the LD Micro conference on June 4th. Audio here and presentation here . The money will be used for acquisitions if something attractive comes up. By the way, this was a non-deal roadshow at LD Micro which means the company is now actively marketing its stock so that big money managers will buy on the open market. As you can see from the price action on June 4th, that has already started as SMSI had its largest volume green day in over a year.
What's more, SMSI just revealed yesterday that TMobile ( TMUS ) in Albania is already a customer and they have high confidence that the recent merger announcement will result in TMUS also adopting the SafePath platform for their customer base as well! As the CEO said yesterday, that will instantly double their business (and in my view can lead to price targets of $30+).
Risks The story is compelling and I don't believe there are any near-term risks to SMSI turning profitable. Q2 will be near break-even and Q3 will be profitable as Sprint ramps up their sales activity. However, in the very long-term I see two risks. First, SMSI does not deal directly with the customer and they are not marketing their own brand. Sprint sells the product as Safe & Found and each carrier who joins may rebrand the product however way they like. It's a shame that if SMSI had millions of customers, the end-consumer won't even know it. If something happened with their relationship with the carriers, SMSI won't be able to sell their service directly to customers. The second risk is that Apple ( AAPL ) and Google ( GOOGL ) can build these safety features into their operating systems over time making these services redundant by SMSI but so far, SMSI is far ahead in features, they keep on innovating, and the service providers are motivated to market the service as it makes it harder for the customer to switch to another carrier. These risks don't change the short-term story but you should be aware of them.
Conclusion Many of us lost a lot of money in HMNY but there is no reason we need to make the money back on the same stock. There are many good investments out there and SMSI, BURG, and AEHR are three good choices at an inflection point. As I noted above, SMSI is closest to seeing these catalysts come through on the bottom line. As the CEO said yesterday at the conference, "You see our stock price, none of this is priced in yet. This is the moment."
